chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ibrahim, from a group of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Amawi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced three [times] in one sitting. He said, 'As for me, I consider that it has become binding [i.e., three divorces are effective], and as for my father [Imam al-Sadiq], he considered that to be one [divorce].'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Imam al-Sadiq and his father regarding three divorces in one sitting?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the jurisprudential divergence between Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) and his father, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), regarding whether triple divorce pronounced in one sitting counts as three or one. This distinction is central to the Shia school's preference for the 'one divorce' view, contrasting with the Sunni majority opinion that treats it as three, and underscores the importance of contextual interpretation in marital law.
